env.docs: Verbosity, as `tracing` directives — `info`, `tankovault_api=debug,info`. Read by `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env`, which is consulted *before* `telemetry.log_filter` and wins over it when set.
env.name: RUST_LOG

bind_addr.description: Listen address for `/v1/render`, `/v1/solve` and the probes. Internal-tier only.

name.description: The name peers know this service by; must match the key they list it under.

token.description:
Presented to peers under `identity = "token"`. Ignored under `mtls`, where the client
certificate is the credential.

san.description:
The client-certificate subject alternative name this peer presents under
`identity = "mtls"`, e.g. `api.tankovault.svc`.

token.description: The token this peer presents under `identity = "token"`.

peers.description: Which services may call this one, keyed by caller name.

ca.description: PEM bundle of the authorities a peer certificate must chain to.

cert.description: PEM certificate chain this service serves and presents.

probe_listen.description:
Address the credential-free `/health` and `/ready` probes bind to, in **plaintext**, on
their own listener (default `0.0.0.0:9091`). Read under `mtls` only.

An orchestrator probe presents no client certificate, so on the mTLS port its plain
`GET` is answered with a TLS alert rather than a response and the replica is restarted
as unhealthy. `null` drops the listener, which is right only where whatever does the
probing *can* present a certificate.

token.description:
The retired tier-wide shared secret. Present only so a deployment that still sets it is
told what to do instead; see [`InternalAuthConfig::resolve`].

enabled.description:
Install the Prometheus recorder and serve the scrape endpoint. When `false` the
scrape route answers `404` and no measurements are retained.

http_requests.description:
Also record per-request HTTP metrics. Separate from [`Self::enabled`]: the request
histogram is the expensive, high-cardinality part.

listen.description:
Address the scrape endpoint binds to on its **own** listener (default `0.0.0.0:9090`),
isolated from the service's public port. `None` merges it onto the primary port.

route.description: Path the scrape endpoint is mounted at.

burst.description: Bucket depth: the most requests a client may spend back-to-back.

per_minute.description: Sustained requests allowed per minute per client key; the bucket's refill rate.

enabled.description: Enforce limits. When `false` the layer is not mounted at all (no per-request cost).

burst.description: Bucket depth: the most requests a client may spend back-to-back.

per_minute.description: Sustained requests allowed per minute per client key; the bucket's refill rate.

burst.description: Bucket depth: the most requests a client may spend back-to-back.

per_minute.description: Sustained requests allowed per minute per client key; the bucket's refill rate.

trust_forwarded_for.description:
Trust `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP` for the client key. **Only behind a reverse proxy
that overwrites these** — otherwise any client can forge a fresh identity and bypass
the limiter.

challenge_wait_ms.description: Extra settle time to let a bot-management challenge clear during `/v1/solve` (ms).

chrome_path.description: Explicit Chrome/Chromium executable path. When `None`, `chromiumoxide` auto-detects.

default_wait_ms.description: Extra settle delay applied after navigation on every `/v1/render` (ms).

headless.description: Run the browser headless (the default; set `false` only for local debugging).

nav_timeout_ms.description: Per-navigation time budget handed to the CDP client (ms).

no_sandbox.description: Pass `--no-sandbox` (required to run Chromium as root inside the runtime container).

session_ttl_secs.description: TTL attached to a solved session when acting as a `ChallengeSolver` back-end (s).

user_agent.description:
User-agent override, applied to the page and reported back so a solved
`cf_clearance` cookie stays paired with a stable UA.

allow_credentials.description:
Allow credentialed cross-origin requests (cookies, `Authorization`). Cannot combine
with a wildcard origin.

allowed_origins.description: Exact origins allowed, e.g. `https://app.example.com`. Empty disables CORS entirely.

expose_api_docs.description:
Serve the browsable API docs (`/scalar`) and the `OpenAPI` document.

Defaults off in production, on elsewhere (hence a function, not a literal): left on,
it hands an attacker the whole admin surface — every `/v1/admin/*` path, the
permission vocabulary, exact request bodies — with no failed probe.

hsts.description:
Emit `Strict-Transport-Security`; meaningless without TLS (browsers ignore it over
plain HTTP).

hsts_max_age_secs.description: `max-age` for the HSTS header, seconds (default: two years, the preload minimum).

max_body_bytes.description: Reject request bodies larger than this, in bytes, before they are buffered.

request_timeout_secs.description: Abort a request that has not produced a response within this many seconds.

security_headers.description:
Send the baseline set of hardening headers (`X-Content-Type-Options`,
`X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy`).

trust_request_id.description:
Accept an inbound `X-Request-Id` instead of minting one. Requires a trusted proxy —
a client-supplied id could otherwise poison log correlation.

json_logs.description: Emit structured JSON logs (production) vs. pretty logs (dev).

log_filter.description:
**`TANKOVAULT_TELEMETRY__OTLP_ENDPOINT` is removed** (it silently did nothing); setting
it is now a hard config error. Re-add only with a real `OpenTelemetryLayer`.

`RUST_LOG`-style filter (e.g. `info,tankovault=debug`).

attach_stacktraces.description: Attach a stack trace to events that carry none of their own.

breadcrumb_level.description:
Least severe `tracing` level kept as a **breadcrumb** — the trail attached to the next
issue. Records at or above [`Self::capture_level`] become issues instead.

capture_level.description: Least severe `tracing` level reported as a Sentry **issue**.

debug.description: Print the SDK's own diagnostics to stderr. For proving a DSN works, not for running.

dsn.description:
Ingest URL, `https://<key>@<host>/<project>`.

A [`SecretString`]: the embedded key is a bearer credential for the project's ingest
endpoint, and this struct is nested in a `TelemetryConfig` that is logged with `?`.
Absent while [`Self::enabled`] is set is a boot failure, not a silent no-op.

enabled.description:
Initialise the Sentry client. `false` installs no client, no panic hook and no layer,
so every other key here is inert and nothing is sent anywhere.

environment.description:
Environment tag on every event. Defaults to `production` under
`TANKOVAULT_PROFILE=production` and `development` otherwise.

http_transactions.description:
Record request spans through the shared HTTP stack: one Sentry transaction per
request, named by the *matched route* rather than the URI, so an id in the path does
not become its own transaction name.

Whether a started transaction is *kept* is [`Self::traces_sample_rate`]'s decision.
This is the switch for a service that should stay out of traces entirely.

max_breadcrumbs.description: How many breadcrumbs one event carries.

release.description:
Release tag on every event; defaults to the workspace version the binary was built
from, which is what makes a regression attributable to a deploy.

sample_rate.description:
Fraction of captured events actually sent, `0.0`-`1.0`. A blunt volume cap — it drops
whole issues, not repetitions of one — so leave it at `1.0` unless quota forces it.

send_default_pii.description:
Send personally identifying data with every event: the client IP, the full request
header set (`Authorization` and `Cookie` included) and the resolved user.

**Off, and worth leaving off.** A reader's IP address and session cookie are exactly
what a crash report does not need in order to be actionable, and Sentry is a third
party for the purposes of the data policy this deployment publishes. On, it also
widens what the HTTP middleware records, because `sentry-tower` reads this same flag
to decide whether to redact sensitive headers.

server_name.description:
Host tag on every event. Left unset, Sentry reports none: the hostname of a replica is
infrastructure detail that [`Self::send_default_pii`] would otherwise gate.

shutdown_timeout_secs.description: How long process exit waits for queued events to drain.

span_attributes.description:
Copy `tracing` span fields onto the Sentry span as attributes. Off: span fields in
this workspace routinely carry ids and user-supplied titles, and a transaction is
stored under a longer retention than a log line.

traces_sample_rate.description:
Fraction of traces this service **starts** that are recorded, `0.0`-`1.0`.

`0.0` (the default) means it starts none of its own. It does **not** mean this service
is absent from a trace: a request or a broker message arriving with a trace already
sampled is continued regardless, which is what keeps one reader action readable across
the whole tier rather than ending at the first service configured differently. Set it
uniformly anyway — `0.05`-`0.2` is an ordinary production figure — since the service
that *starts* a trace is the one whose rate decides whether it exists at all.

service_name.description: Logical service name reported in traces/metrics.
